content: 1. Administer 30 mg of primaquine orally once daily for 14 days. This regimen should be used in combination with chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine. 2. For patients with mild G6PD deficiency or as an alternative to the daily regimen, administer 45 mg of primaquine orally once weekly for 8 weeks. This alternative regimen should only be used after consultation with an infectious disease or tropical medicine expert. 3. For the treatment of Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium ovale malaria, administer 30 mg of primaquine orally once daily for 14 days after leaving a malaria-endemic area. 4. When used in combination with clindamycin for malaria prophylaxis, administer 5 mg/kg of primaquine orally once daily (maximum dose: 30 mg/day). Begin treatment 1–2 days prior to travel and continue for 7 days after leaving the malaria-endemic area. 5. Primaquine and dronedarone both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated due to the risk of arrhythmias. 6. Lefamulin increases the levels or effects of primaquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Lefamulin is contraindicated with CYP3A substrates known to prolong the QT interval. 8. Primaquine and thioridazine both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated. 9. Primaquine and amiodarone both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 10. Primaquine and amisulpride both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, ECG monitoring is recommended. 11. Primaquine and anagrelide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 12. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of primaquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 13. Co-administration of apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, with drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates can result in reduced therapeutic efficacy. If coadministration is unavoidable, evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose as needed. 14. Primaquine and arsenic trioxide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 15. Primaquine and asenapine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 16. Primaquine and azithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 17. Primaquine and bedaquiline both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 18. Primaquine and buprenorphine (including buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, and long-acting injection formulations) all prolong the QTc interval. Avoid these combinations or use alternative drugs. 19. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of primaquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 20. Ceritinib and primaquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 21. Chloroquine and primaquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 22. Primaquine and chlorpromazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 23. Citalopram and primaquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 24. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of primaquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 25. Crizotinib and primaquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 26. Avoid coadministration of topical dapsone with oral dapsone or antimalarial medications due to the potential for hemolytic reactions. 27. Deferiprone and primaquine increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor absolute neutrophil count more frequently due to the risk of neutropenia or agranulocytosis. 28. Desflurane and primaquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 29. Primaquine and disopyramide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 30. Primaquine and dofetilide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug.
